newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end moderately higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end moderately higher.

text.p: June 11 - U.S. stock index futures ended moderately higher. June S&Ps closed at fourth consecutive record settle, stayed shy of all-time peak of 872.25. Some said market still skewed to upside despite overbought condition. Late trade spotty before Thursday's May US retail sales, seen up 0.4 pct, up 0.3 pct ex-autos. Sept S&P 500s take lead-month position Thursday.

Some brokers noted vague signs during the afternoon of asset allocation plays and said portfolios looked as though they were rotating equity holdings by sector. Some also noted dealer selling in Treasury bonds and buying of stocks.
"It traded like a big portfolio adjustment, maybe sectional rotation," said one S&P 500s futures floor analyst.

Still, firmness in Treasury bond futures generally helped offset the dollar's renewed decline, while an afternoon turn back up in over-the-counter stocks following a morning pullback also released stock futures from downward pressure, brokers added.
Turnover dwindled late as traders waited for Thursday's May U.S. retail sales figures, expected to show a 0.4 percent increase and a 0.3 percent gain without autos.
Sentiment still favored the long side, and even some traders who had searched for selling opportunities said they gave up early when June S&P 500s proved extremely resilient on the day's lows.
September S&P 500s become new lead-contract month Thursday in the trading pit, although the rollover activity slowed Wednesday afternoon from its brisk pace earlier this week, they said.

June S&P 500s ended up 1.85 points at 870.55, September S&Ps rose 1.80 to 879.40, Nikkei fell 140.0 to 20,405.0, Midcaps firmed 0.15 to 283.90, NYSE Composite rose 1.15 to 454.35, Russell lost 0.45 to 389.55, and Nasdaq rose 6.50 to 950.75.
